mainTopic: The list of טפח measurements, and when an afterbirth (שליא) is linked to a baby
overview: רבי אושעיא taught a list of five things measured as a טפח, and the גמרא tests whether other cases belong on it. Toy ovens for girls and a stone sticking out of an oven are left off because both are disputed rules. The frame of the שולחן is left off because its size is written in the Torah. The כפורת is left off because it is a holy item, and the beam over an alleyway is left off because it is only דרבנן. So the list covers only Torah rules whose size the Torah does not state. Next, רב teaches when a שליא that comes out after a birth is linked to the baby, and when we worry it came from another baby. רב כהנא raises a contradiction between two of רב's statements, and it is resolved by telling apart a נפל and a healthy baby. A story with שמואל confirms רב's rule that a שליא is linked only to a baby that could live. Finally, רבי יוסי בן שאול asks רבי about a crow-shaped discharge with a שליא and challenges רבי's answer from a ברייתא; that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Toy ovens are also a handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's list of five טפח measurements, because toy ovens for girls are also measured as a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But toy ovens for girls are also a handbreadth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging רבי אושעיא's list of five things measured as a טפח. It points to one more case: toy ovens that girls play with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא presented his list as if those five were the only things measured as a טפח. If toy ovens also have a measure of a טפח, the list looks incomplete. The next steps bring the source showing that toy ovens really are a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Small toy ovens that girls play with
A handbreadth, a measure of about one hand's width

phrases.english: Toy ovens of girls are a handbreadth!
phrases.notes: Read this as: why didn't רבי אושעיא add this case to his list of five handbreadth measures?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of challenges against רבי אושעיא's list of five טפח measures.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's list of exactly five things measured as a טפח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The toy oven is another case measured as a טפח, so the list seems to be missing an item.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: an oven needs four handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the source for its challenge. In that ברייתא, רבי מאיר says a whole oven, and a broken piece of one, needs to be four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: an oven in its original state is four handbreadths, and its remains are four handbreadths. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing the source behind the challenge. First it quotes רבי מאיר's view on the size of an oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a new oven must be four טפחים tall before it can become טמא. A broken piece of an oven that was already טמא stays טמא only if that piece is four טפחים. This view does not yet mention a טפח; the next step brings the חכמים, who do.

keyTerms.meaning: Its original state, when the oven is whole and new
Its remains, the broken pieces left after the oven breaks

phrases.english: As it is taught:
An oven in its original state is four,
phrases.notes: Four means four handbreadths tall. That is the size it needs before it can become טמא.

phrases.english: and its remains are four,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source that backs up the challenge in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that toy ovens are measured as a טפח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the size of ovens, starting with רבי מאיר's view

steps.title: The חכמים: a small oven can be any size
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the four-טפח rule applies only to a large oven. A small oven can become טמא at any size once it is finished, and a broken piece stays טמא if it is most of the oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: when was this said? About a large oven. But a small oven, in its original state, is any size once its construction is finished, and its remains need most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the חכמים, who disagree with רבי מאיר about small ovens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים limit רבי מאיר's four-טפח rule to a large oven made for real use. A small oven can become טמא at any size, as soon as it is fully made. A broken piece of a small oven stays טמא only if it is most of the oven. The words 'any size' are about to be defined in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case were these words said? This limits a rule to certain cases.
Any size at all
Once its making is completed
Most of it, the majority

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'any size' as truly zero size. The next step tells you that רבי ינאי gives it a real measure: one טפח.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
In what case were these words said? With a large one,
but with a small one —
its original state is any size
once its construction is completed,
and its remains need the majority of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the חכמים's view, which disagrees with רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That a small oven has its own, smaller measure

steps.title: How small is 'any size'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'any size' means for a small oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'any size'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact measure behind the חכמים's words 'any size'. This sets up רבי ינאי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any size' sounds as if there is no minimum at all. The גמרא wants to know whether there is still some smallest size. The answer is what ties toy ovens to the טפח measure.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much is 'any size'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in the חכמים's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact smallest size of a small oven that can become טמא

steps.title: רבי ינאי: one handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי says 'any size' means one טפח, because toy ovens for girls are made one טפח tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: a handbreadth, because people make toy ovens for girls one handbreadth tall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי answers that 'any size' means one טפח. This completes the proof that toy ovens have a טפח measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure comes from real life: toy ovens for girls were made one טפח tall. So according to the חכמים, a small oven that is one טפח can become טמא. This gives a sixth 'טפח' case that רבי אושעיא did not list, and the challenge from step 1 is now fully backed up.

keyTerms.meaning: Because that is how people make them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said: A handbreadth,
as they make toy ovens for girls a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about what 'any size' means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Any size' means one טפח, the usual height of a toy oven.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא only lists undisputed rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אושעיא did not include rules that are the subject of a מחלוקת, and the toy-oven measure is one of those.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is not dealing with disputed cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 1. רבי אושעיא's list only includes rules that everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The toy-oven טפח comes only from the חכמים's view, and רבי מאיר disagrees. Since it is a מחלוקת, it does not belong on a list of fixed, agreed-on measures. The list is therefore not missing anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute, a case where Sages disagree
He is not talking about

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא's list of five טפח measures only includes rules that no one disputes.

phrases.english: He is not speaking about a dispute.
phrases.notes: He is רבי אושעיא. The toy oven is a dispute between רבי מאיר and the חכמים, so he left it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised in step 1 and backed up in steps 2 to 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אושעיא's list seemed to include every case measured as a טפח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only includes undisputed measures, and the toy oven is disputed.

steps.title: The same answer works for the stone
steps.stepSummary: Now that the גמרא has this answer, it says the stone sticking out of an oven is also a disputed rule, so it too was left off the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, this too is a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes its new answer and uses it for the earlier challenge about a stone sticking out of an oven. It says that rule is also disputed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא had challenged רבי אושעיא from a stone that sticks out of an oven one טפח. Now there is a simpler way to explain why he left it out: that rule is also a מחלוקת. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this answer
This one too

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,
this too is a dispute.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the earlier case of a stone sticking out of an oven one handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דַאֲתֵית לְהָכִי, הָא נָמֵי פְּלוּגְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer from step 6 and applies it to the earlier challenge about the stone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a newly found principle to an earlier challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stone sticking out of an oven needed its own separate answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stone is also a disputed rule, so the same answer covers it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה disagrees about the stone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the stone rule is disputed. The end of the same teaching quotes רבי יהודה, who says the טפח rule applies only to a stone that sticks out toward the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the end of that teaching says: רבי יהודה said, they said a handbreadth only for a stone sticking out from the oven toward the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that the stone rule is a מחלוקת. רבי יהודה limits the טפח rule to a stone pointing toward the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gives the stone a measure of one טפח. רבי יהודה says that measure applies only when the stone points toward the wall, not toward the open room. Since he limits the rule, it is a disputed rule, and that explains why רבי אושעיא did not list it.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching
They said it only for a certain case
Wall

steps.whatToRemember: Both the toy oven and the stone sticking out of an oven are disputed rules, so neither belongs on רבי אושעיא's list of five agreed-on טפח measures.

phrases.english: As the latter clause teaches:
Rabbi Yehuda said:
They did not say a handbreadth
except from the oven toward the wall.
phrases.notes: He means a stone sticking out of the oven on the side that faces the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in step 7 that the stone rule is disputed.
steps.raayaObject: That the טפח rule for a stone sticking out of an oven is disputed
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's statement at the end of the same teaching

steps.title: What about the frame of the Table?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's list. The מסגרת of the שולחן is also one טפח, so why is it missing?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the frame of the Table, which is one handbreadth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds another rule measured by one טפח that רבי אושעיא did not put on his list. It asks why he left it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 6 explained why disputed rules were left off. The מסגרת of the שולחן in the משכן is not disputed, so that answer does not explain why it is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is also. This is a challenge that points to a case that was left out.
The frame or border around the שולחן in the משכן
The Table in the משכן or the בית המקדש that held the לחם הפנים

phrases.english: But there is the frame, which is a handbreadth!
phrases.notes: This is the frame of the שולחן. Its size is in שמות 25:25.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stone case is settled, the גמרא brings another טפח rule that is missing from the list.
steps.kashyaTarget: How complete רבי אושעיא's list is
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The frame is a טפח rule that nobody disputes, yet it is not on the list.

steps.title: He does not list things written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא does not include measures that the Torah states openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is not dealing with things that are written in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the frame's size is written right in the פסוק. רבי אושעיא's list does not include things like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His list only covers טפח rules that someone had to know from outside the פסוק. The frame's measure is stated openly in the Torah, so there was nothing new to teach about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that are written in the Torah
He is not dealing with this. It shows what the list does not cover.

phrases.english: He is not dealing with things that are written.
phrases.notes: He means things whose size the Torah itself states.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the frame.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list includes every rule measured by a טפח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list leaves out measures that the Torah states openly.

steps.title: What about the Ark Cover?
steps.stepSummary: The כפורת is one טפח thick, and the Torah does not state that size. So why is it missing from the list?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the Ark Cover, which is a handbreadth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case that the last answer does not explain. The כפורת is one טפח thick, but that number is not written in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer left out things whose size is written in the Torah. The כפורת's thickness is not written, so the problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold cover on top of the ארון in the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: But there is the Ark Cover, which is a handbreadth!
phrases.notes: The Torah gives its length and width, but not how thick it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the narrower definition from step 10 with a new case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The thickness of the כפורת is a טפח that is not written in the Torah, so it should be on the list.

steps.title: He does not list holy items
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא's list does not deal with קדשים, the holy items of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is not dealing with holy items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כפורת is a holy item. רבי אושעיא's list does not cover holy items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the list is narrowed a second time. Measures of holy Temple items are left out, even when the Torah does not state their size.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy items, here meaning the objects of the משכן or the בית המקדש

phrases.english: He is not dealing with holy items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the כפורת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any טפח measure not written in the Torah would be on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Holy items are left out too.

steps.title: What about the beam over an alleyway?
steps.stepSummary: A קורה for an alleyway on שבת only needs to be one טפח wide. Why is this not on the list?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the rule that it is enough for the beam to be a handbreadth wide!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third case. It is not written in the Torah and it is not a holy item: the beam over an alleyway that allows carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case gets past both earlier answers. The beam's size is not written in the Torah, and the beam is not holy. So why did רבי אושעיא leave it out?

keyTerms.meaning: A beam placed across the entrance of an alleyway (מבוי) so that people may carry there on שבת
It is enough for it. This tells us the minimum size needed.

phrases.english: But there is the rule that it is enough for the beam
phrases.notes: This is the beam over an alleyway entrance that lets people carry there on שבת.

phrases.english: to be a handbreadth wide!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא דַּיָּהּ לַקּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא רְחָבָה טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a case that neither of the two earlier answers covers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list as narrowed in steps 10 and 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The beam is not written in the Torah and is not holy, so it should be on the list.

steps.title: His list is only Torah rules whose size the Torah does not state
steps.stepSummary: Rules that are דרבנן are left out. The list covers only things in the Torah whose measure the Torah does not give.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is not dealing with rabbinic laws. He is dealing only with things that are written in the Torah but whose measures are not stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the beam is only a rule דרבנן. Then it states clearly what kind of rules רבי אושעיא's list does cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This last answer pulls together everything from steps 10 to 14. The list covers rules that come from the Torah, but where the Torah does not say the size and the טפח is known from outside the פסוק. That is why written measures, holy items, and rabbinic rules are all left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules made by the Rabbis, not from the Torah
They are not stated openly
Their measures or sizes

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא's list covers only Torah rules whose טפח size the Torah does not state. Rules about holy items and rabbinic rules are not on it.

phrases.english: He is not dealing with rabbinic laws.
Rather, he is dealing with things that are written
but whose measures are not stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּדְרַבָּנַן לָא קָמַיְירֵי אֶלָּא בְּדִכְתִיבָן וְלָא מְפָרְשִׁי שִׁיעוּרַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the beam challenge and gives the full definition of the list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what the list covers, then defining it in full
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any טפח rule that is not written in the Torah and not holy would be on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only Torah rules whose size the Torah does not state are on the list.

steps.title: רב on an afterbirth that comes out after a birth
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא quotes רב. For the first three days, an afterbirth is linked to the baby already born. After that, we worry it came from another baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא sat before רב כהנא and said in the name of רב יהודה, quoting רב: During all of the first three days, we link the afterbirth to the baby. From then on, we are concerned that there was another baby.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב teaches what to do when a woman passes a שליא after she has given birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the first three days, we say the שליא belongs to the baby that was already born, so there is no new birth to worry about. After three days, we have to worry that a second baby came out with it, and the rules of a woman who gave birth apply again.

keyTerms.meaning: The afterbirth, the sac that the baby develops in
We link it to. We say it comes from a known cause.
We are concerned about, and we act strictly because of it
From this point on

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta sat
before Rav Kahana,
and he sat and said:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
During all of the first three days
phrases.notes: He means the first three days after the woman gave birth.

phrases.english: we link the afterbirth to the baby.
From then on,
we are concerned about another baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section about the שליא begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For three days after a birth, an afterbirth is linked to the baby already born. After that, we worry it came from a second baby.

steps.title: Did רב really say that?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא points to a different statement of רב: a second baby does not stay in the womb at all after the first is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did רב really say this? But רב said that a baby does not stay behind after its twin at all!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges the teaching. He uses another statement of רב that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a second baby never stays behind after the first, then a second baby could not come out three days later. That makes the worry 'after three days' strange, so the two statements of רב seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רב really say this? This opens a contradiction between two of a sage's statements.
Stays behind, is delayed
Its companion. Here it means the twin born first.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב כהנא is speaking to רב יצחק.

phrases.english: Did Rav really say this?
But Rav said:
A baby does not stay behind
after its twin at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי וְהָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's three-day rule about the שליא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב also said a second baby never stays behind after the first, so a baby could not come out three days later.

steps.title: Maybe one statement is about a נפל and the other about a בן קיימא
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק is silent. רב כהנא suggests that one statement is about a baby that could not live, and the other is about a healthy baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent. He said to him: Perhaps here it is about a non-viable baby, and there it is about a viable baby?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק has no answer. So רב כהנא offers a possible way to fit both statements of רב together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first baby is a נפל, a second baby can come out even days later, so the three-day worry makes sense. When the first baby is a בן קיימא, a second baby does not stay behind at all. Each statement is about a different case, so they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent. He had no answer.
Perhaps. It offers a possible answer.
A baby that cannot survive
A healthy baby that can survive

steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is the one who asked the question, and he is also the one who suggests this answer, not רב יצחק. The word 'perhaps' shows it is offered as a possibility.

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: רב יצחק had no answer to the question.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רב כהנא suggests the answer himself.

phrases.english: Perhaps here it is about a non-viable baby,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the three-day rule. A second baby can come later when the first is a נפל.

phrases.english: and there it is about a viable baby?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כָּאן בְּנֵפֶל כָּאן בְּבֶן קַיָּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each statement is about a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements of רב are about the same kind of birth, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three-day rule is about a first baby that is a נפל. 'No delay' is about a first baby that is a בן קיימא.

steps.title: רב said this split outright
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק tells רב כהנא that his answer is exactly what רב said. After a נפל, the afterbirth is linked to it for three days. After a healthy birth, it is linked to the baby for up to ten days.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you telling me רב's teaching as your own idea? רב said it outright. If she miscarried a baby that could not live and later discharged an afterbirth, for three days we link the afterbirth to that baby. After that, we worry there was another baby. If she gave birth to a healthy baby and later discharged an afterbirth, even up to ten days later we do not worry about another baby.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק confirms that רב כהנא's answer from step 17 is not just a guess. רב himself said it clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, רב כהנא suggested that רב's two statements are about two different kinds of births. Now we hear that רב actually said this split himself. After a נפל, we link the afterbirth to it for only three days. After a healthy birth, we link it for a full ten days, so the two statements do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, said outright
We are concerned there was another baby
Ten days, how long after a healthy birth the afterbirth is still linked to the baby

steps.whatToRemember: After a נפל, the afterbirth is linked to it for three days. After a healthy birth, it is linked to the baby for ten days. רב himself taught both of these rules.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether we worry about another baby decides whether the woman may have to keep the laws of a new birth.

phrases.english: He said to him: Are you saying
Rav's teaching (as your own idea)?
phrases.notes: רב יצחק is speaking to רב כהנא. He means: no need to guess, because רב said it himself.

phrases.english: Rav said it outright, like this:
If she miscarried a baby that could not live
and afterward discharged an afterbirth,
for all three days
we link the afterbirth to that baby;
from then on
we worry about another baby.
If she gave birth and afterward discharged an afterbirth,
even from now until ten days
we do not worry about another baby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the answer רב כהנא suggested in step 17 by quoting רב's own explicit words.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's split between a נפל and a healthy baby
steps.raayaSupportSource: An explicit statement of רב, passed on by רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא

steps.title: שמואל sees רב יוסף hurrying toward them
steps.stepSummary: A story begins. שמואל, רב's students and רב יהודה are sitting together. רב יוסף בריה דרב מנשיא מדויל hurries toward them, and שמואל jokes that the smallest push knocks this man down.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל, the students of רב, and רב יהודה were sitting together. רב יוסף, son of רב מנשיא from דויל, was passing by and hurrying toward them. שמואל said: Here comes a man you can knock over with a stalk of wheat, and he falls and stays down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will bring out another teaching of רב about a שליא. This step only sets the scene for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's joke means that רב יוסף cannot stand up to even a small challenge. The scene is set so that שמואל will question him about רב's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Hurrying and coming
A stalk or straw of wheat
Falls down and stays pushed down

phrases.english: Shmuel and the students of Rav
and Rav Yehuda were sitting.
Rav Yosef was passing by and walking,
son of Rav Menashya from D'vil,
toward them, hurrying along.
He (Shmuel) said: A man is coming to us
whom we can knock over with a stalk of wheat,
and he falls and stays down.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל וְתַלְמִידִי דְּרַב וְרַב יְהוּדָה הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story that will bring out another teaching of רב about an afterbirth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. The scene is set for שמואל to question רב יוסף.

steps.title: שמואל asks what רב said about an afterbirth
steps.stepSummary: When רב יוסף arrives, שמואל asks him what רב taught about a שליא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile he arrived. שמואל said to him: What did רב say about an afterbirth?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל tests רב יוסף with a question about רב's teaching. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל expects רב יוסף to fail. The question is about רב's rule for linking a שליא to a baby, which is the topic we have been learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, in the middle of this

phrases.english: Meanwhile he arrived.
Shmuel said to him:
What did Rav say about an afterbirth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The man described in step 19 arrives, and שמואל questions him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רב ruled about linking an afterbirth to a baby

steps.title: Only link an afterbirth to a baby that could live
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that רב said: we link a שליא only to a דבר של קיימא, a baby that could live.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב said: we only link an afterbirth to something that could live.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives שמואל רב's rule. An afterbirth is linked only to a baby that could live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a short version of the rule from step 18. After a healthy baby, the afterbirth is simply linked to that baby. A נפל does not get this full link, which is why after three days we worry about another baby.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that lasts, meaning a baby that could live
Only, nothing except

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav said:
We do not link the afterbirth
except to something that could live.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב: אֵין תּוֹלִין אֶת הַשִּׁלְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב taught that an afterbirth is linked only to a baby that could live.

steps.title: רב's students confirm the teaching
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asks all of רב's students, and they confirm the rule. Then שמואל looks harshly at רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל asked all of רב's students, and they told him: Yes, that is right. Then he looked at רב יהודה angrily.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל checks רב יוסף's answer with רב's other students, and they confirm it. The story ends with שמואל looking angrily at רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man שמואל expected to fall turns out to know רב's teaching correctly. רב יהודה was also a student of רב, and it seems שמואל was upset with him about this teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked them
He looked at him harshly

steps.whatToRemember: רב's students confirm the rule: an afterbirth is linked only to a baby that could live.

phrases.english: Shmuel asked
all of Rav's students,
and they said to him: That's right.
Then he looked at Rav Yehuda harshly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the answer from step 21.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's report of רב's rule

steps.title: A crow-shaped birth with an afterbirth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן שאול asks רבי about a woman who discharges something shaped like a crow along with an afterbirth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן שאול asked רבי: A woman who discharges something shaped like a crow, and also an afterbirth: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question starts. Can an afterbirth be linked to a discharged shape that looks like a bird?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the afterbirth was linked to a human baby. Here the discharged thing looks like a crow, so we must ask whether the afterbirth can be linked to it, or whether we worry there was another baby.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries or discharges something
The shape of a crow
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל מֵרַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul asked Rabbi:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: A woman who discharges the shape of a crow
and an afterbirth: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל מֵרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question on the same topic of linking an afterbirth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an afterbirth can be linked to a discharged crow-shaped form

steps.title: Only link it to a species that has an afterbirth
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that we link an afterbirth only to something whose species has an afterbirth.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We only link it to something whose kind has an afterbirth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rules that the afterbirth cannot be linked to the crow shape. The reason is that its species does not have an afterbirth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds do not have an afterbirth, so the afterbirth cannot belong to the crow shape. Because of this, we cannot explain the afterbirth away by linking it to the crow.

keyTerms.meaning: In its species, in its kind

steps.whatToRemember: An afterbirth is linked only to a birth whose species has an afterbirth.

phrases.english: He said to him: We do not link it
except to something
whose species has an afterbirth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין תּוֹלִין אֶלָּא בְּדָבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּמִינוֹ שִׁלְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי בן שאול's question from step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The afterbirth is not linked to the crow shape, because crows have no afterbirth.

steps.title: What if the afterbirth is attached to the crow-shaped discharge?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן שאול follows up: what is the law if the שליא is physically tied to the crow-shaped thing?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the afterbirth is tied to it, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בן שאול asks a follow-up question about the case of the crow-shaped discharge. Now the afterbirth is physically attached to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, רבי said we only link an afterbirth to something whose species has an afterbirth, and a crow does not. But if the afterbirth is physically tied to the crow-shape, it seems hard to say they are unrelated. So the question is whether the physical attachment changes the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Tied or attached

phrases.english: If it is tied to it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "It" is the afterbirth, and it is tied to the crow-shaped thing from the last question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question that tests רבי's rule from step 24 against a harder case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether physical attachment of the שליא to a non-human form makes us link the afterbirth to that form

steps.title: רבי says such a case does not exist
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that the question is about something that never happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You asked about something that does not exist.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers that the case is not real. An afterbirth is never actually attached to a crow-shaped discharge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי does not give a ruling for the case. He says the case cannot happen. This fits his rule in step 24: a species with no afterbirth cannot have one attached to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that does not exist or never happens
You asked

phrases.english: He said to him: You asked about a thing that does not exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by saying its case never happens
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An afterbirth attached to a crow-shaped discharge is an impossible case, so no ruling is needed

steps.title: A ברייתא describes an afterbirth tied to an animal or bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן שאול objects from a ברייתא that speaks of an afterbirth tied to an animal-shaped or bird-shaped discharge. This suggests the case does exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: A woman who discharges a kind of domesticated animal, wild animal, or bird, and an afterbirth comes with them: when the afterbirth is tied to them, we do not worry about another baby. When the afterbirth is not tied to them, we worry about another baby. I impose upon them…
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בן שאול challenges רבי's answer by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא openly talks about an afterbirth tied to an animal or bird shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said an afterbirth attached to a non-human form never happens. The ברייתא gives rules for exactly that case. If it is tied, we assume the afterbirth belongs to the animal-shape. If it is not tied, we worry there was a different baby inside. So the case seems real, and this contradicts רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries or discharges something
A domesticated animal, a wild animal, and a bird
We are concerned or we take into account
Another baby (a different fetus)
Impose upon them (a legal stringency)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying a woman gave birth to a real animal. It means a discharge that has the form of an animal or bird, like the crow-shape in step 23.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
A woman who discharges a type of domesticated animal, wild animal, or bird
and an afterbirth with them,
when the afterbirth is tied to them,
we are not concerned about another offspring.
If the afterbirth is not tied to them,
we are concerned about another offspring.
and I impose upon them

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: הַמַּפֶּלֶת מִין בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי's answer in step 26 using a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's claim in step 26 that an afterbirth attached to a non-human form never happens
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives a ruling for an afterbirth tied to an animal-shaped or bird-shaped discharge, so the case must exist
